# @r4pm/components

> React components for process mining: Petri nets, object-centric Petri nets, directly-follows
> graphs, dotted charts, alignments, OCEL summaries, process trees, log editors, and the pieces the
> viewers are built from. Peer deps: react >= 18, react-dom >= 18. License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

This is the condensed reference for coding agents. `scripts/gen-catalog.mjs` builds the tables
between the generated markers out of the source; the prose around them is hand-written. The
Storybook gallery (`pnpm --filter @r4pm/components dev`) adds live examples and generated props
tables.

## Minimal working setup

All four parts below are required. Anything missing renders as an empty box.

```tsx
import "@r4pm/components/styles.css";                     // 1. stylesheet, once
import { Theme, ViewerConfigProvider, ViewerExportFrame, DFGViewer } from "@r4pm/components";
import { wasmLayout } from "@r4pm/components/rust-layout/wasm";  // 2. a layout engine

export function App({ dfg }) {
  return (
    <Theme>                                                {/* 3. Radix theme wrapper */}
      <ViewerConfigProvider value={{ layout: wasmLayout }}>
        <ViewerExportFrame filename="dfg" style={{ height: 480 }}>  {/* 4. size + export */}
          <DFGViewer data={dfg} />
        </ViewerExportFrame>
      </ViewerConfigProvider>
    </Theme>
  );
}
```

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. **A graph viewer needs a parent with a definite height.** Its root is `height: 100%`. In an
   auto-height parent it collapses to a `min-height` floor or to zero. Inside a flex column the
   wrapper needs `flex: 1; min-height: 0`.
2. **Graph viewers need a `layout` engine.** The core includes none and without one the nodes stack in a
   line. Set it once on `ViewerConfigProvider`. Applies to DFG, OC-DFG, OC-DECLARE, Petri net and
   process tree. The OCEL type graph and extraction blueprint carry their own default.
3. **Image export exists only inside `<ViewerExportFrame>`.** No viewer renders an export control on
   its own. See "Image export" below.
4. **Import UI primitives from `@r4pm/components/ui`**, never from `@radix-ui/themes` directly. The
   package lints this.
5. **`styles.css` or `rules.css`, never both.** Use `rules.css` only when your app runs its own
   Tailwind build, and import it after your Tailwind entry. Preflight resets the controls Radix then
   restyles.
6. **Memoize `colorOf`, `format`, `actions` and the `ViewerConfigProvider` value.** A fresh object
   identity every render makes viewers restyle and relayout.

## Entry points

| Import | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `@r4pm/components` | viewers, primitives, feedback states, `ViewerExportFrame`, and the presentation contract (`ViewerProps`, `ViewerConfig`, `ViewerConfigProvider`, `useViewerConfig`, `colorForKey`, `colorForSeed`) |
| `@r4pm/components/ui` | the Radix Themes seam: `Theme`, `Button`, `Card`, `Combobox`, `CardSelector`, `ConfirmButton`, ... |
| `@r4pm/components/charts` | Plotly-backed viewers: `DottedChart`, `CaseDurationChart`, `EventsPerTimeChart`, `ObjectAttributeChangesChart`, `ActivityChart`, `ThemedPlot` |
| `@r4pm/components/petri` | the React Flow + ELK Petri-net editor |
| `@r4pm/components/process-tree` | the process-tree editor |
| `@r4pm/components/extraction-blueprint` | the extraction blueprint editor |
| `@r4pm/components/elk-layout` | `elkLayout`: pure-JS layout engine (elkjs), no `renderSvg` |
| `@r4pm/components/rust-layout/wasm` | `wasmLayout`: Rust/wasm layout engine, including `renderSvg` |
| `@r4pm/components/styles.css` | precompiled stylesheet (Tailwind + Radix theme + package rules) |
| `@r4pm/components/rules.css` | the same minus Tailwind, for apps with their own Tailwind build |

Heavy viewers sit behind subpaths. Importing `@r4pm/components` never pulls in Plotly or the editors.

## Shared configuration

Set once via `ViewerConfigProvider`. Any viewer overrides any field with a prop of the same name.

```ts
interface ViewerConfig {
  colorOf?: (scope: string, key: string) => string | undefined;
  format?: { number?: (n: number) => string; date?: (ms: number) => string; duration?: (ms: number) => string };
  actions?: ViewerAction[];              // context-menu entries on elements
  alignmentStyle?: "trace" | "deviation";
  onSelect?: (target: ViewerTarget) => void;
  onElementContextMenu?: (target: ViewerTarget, event: { clientX: number; clientY: number }) => void;
  layout?: LayoutEngine;
}

interface ViewerProps<T> extends ViewerConfig { data: T; handle?: string }
type StaticViewerProps<T> = { data: T };   // viewers with no interactive surface
interface ViewerTarget { scope: string; key: string; data?: unknown }
```

`ViewerTarget.scope` values emitted today: `"activity"` (DFG / OC-DFG clicks and context menus) and
`"time-range"` with key `"<startMs>/<endMs>"` (dotted chart selection). Treat it as an open string.

Between provider and prop, `format` merges field by field. The other fields replace wholesale.

## Coloring

Without a `colorOf`, viewers call `colorForKey(scope, key)`, a deterministic OKLCH hash. The same
activity gets the same color in every viewer and across sessions, with no palette to maintain.

```ts
import { colorForKey, colorForSeed, useColorOf, shadeHex, softBadgeStyle, colorToHex } from "@r4pm/components";

colorForKey("activity", "register request"); // deterministic hex
colorForSeed("register request");            // same hash, no scope prefix
useColorOf("activity");                      // hook: scope-bound resolver, never returns undefined
shadeHex(hex, "foreground");                 // readable text shade  ("normal" | "foreground" | "light")
softBadgeStyle(hex);                         // { backgroundColor, color } for a tinted badge
colorToHex("indigo", "light");               // Radix accent name -> hex, same three modes
```

Color scopes in use: `"activity"`, `"objectType"`. Returning `undefined` from `colorOf` falls back to
the hash for that key, which is how partial palettes work.

The shade helpers mix against the CSS system colors `Canvas` and `CanvasText`. They adapt to light
and dark mode with no class detection.

## Image export

`<ViewerExportFrame>` is the only export control in the package. Wrap a viewer, or any content, and a
download menu appears in the corner.

```tsx
<ViewerExportFrame
  filename="dfg"                              // base name; extension appended
  onSave={(bytes, name, mime) => save(bytes)} // optional: take the bytes instead of downloading
  onError={(err) => toast(err)}               // optional; also fires the EXPORT_ERROR_EVENT window event
  menuPlacement="top-right"                   // "top-right" | "top-left" | "bottom-right" | "bottom-left"
  showMenu                                    // false hides the control, keeps the context alive
  style={{ height: 480 }}                     // the frame can be the sizing box
>
  <DFGViewer data={dfg} />
</ViewerExportFrame>
```

The menu offers two routes whenever it can. The viewer's own group (SVG, PNG, JPEG) redraws the
viewer's model as SVG, crisp at any size; its PNG and JPEG entries rasterize that SVG at the chosen
scale (1x, 2x, 4x). The **Screenshot** group (PNG, JPEG) is an html-to-image snapshot of the frame
content, always available, and catches the on-screen chrome the SVG route omits: settings cards,
legend overlays, selection.

Two attributes bound the snapshot. `data-export-root` marks the subtree to capture and defaults to
the whole frame; `data-export-ignore` drops an element from it.

Viewers registering a vector source, and whether a prop can override the key:

<!-- @generated:export-keys -->

| Registry key | `exportKey` prop overrides it | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deviation-alignment-strip` | yes | `src/shared/DeviationAlignmentStrip.tsx` |
| `dfg` | no | `src/dfg/DfgGraph.tsx` |
| `log-variants` | no | `src/log-variants.tsx` |
| `oc-declare` | no | `src/oc-declare/OCDeclareViz.tsx` |
| `ocel-type-graph` | no | `src/ocel-type-graph/OcelTypeGraph.tsx` |
| `ocpn` | yes | `src/object-centric-petri-net.tsx` |
| `ocpn-simulator` | yes | `src/object-centric-petri-net-simulator.tsx` |
| `petri-net` | yes | `src/petri-net.tsx` |
| `petri-net-simulator` | yes | `src/petri-net-simulator.tsx` |
| `process-tree` | yes | `src/process-tree/editor/Editor.tsx` |
| `trace-alignment-strip` | yes | `src/shared/TraceAlignmentStrip.tsx` |

<!-- @end -->

Keys have to be unique within a frame. Two viewers sharing one key collapse into a single menu entry;
`exportKey` separates them. Any component can register its own source:

```tsx
import { useRegisterExport, type VectorExportSource } from "@r4pm/components";

const source = useMemo<VectorExportSource>(() => ({ label: "Throughput", toSvg: () => svgString }), [svgString]);
useRegisterExport("sparkline", source);  // keep `source` identity stable
```

`toSvg` runs at click time and sees current state. Returning `null` while nothing is ready makes the
menu report that instead of downloading an empty file.

## Layout engines

```tsx
import { wasmLayout } from "@r4pm/components/rust-layout/wasm"; // Rust/wasm, orthogonal routing, has renderSvg
import { elkLayout } from "@r4pm/components/elk-layout";        // pure JS (elkjs), spline routing, no renderSvg

<ViewerConfigProvider value={{ layout: wasmLayout }}>...</ViewerConfigProvider>
```

Both load lazily on first layout and stay out of the core bundle. SVG export does not need
`renderSvg`; it falls back to the package's own pure-TS renderer and works on either engine. A host
renderer matches the engine's geometry more exactly.

Per-instance override: `<DFGViewer layoutOverride={fn} renderSvg={fn} />` beats the provider.

Custom transport, to run the Rust engine on your own backend instead of in-browser wasm:

```ts
import { createRustLayout, type LayoutTransport } from "@r4pm/components";

const layout = createRustLayout({
  layoutGraph: (spec) => callBackend("layout_graph", spec),
  rerouteGraph: (spec) => callBackend("reroute_graph", spec),
});
```

## Persisted display settings

Viewers hold small display choices in local state: DFG metric and direction, edge cutoff, export row
limit. `ViewStateProvider` hoists them to the host.

```tsx
<ViewStateProvider viewState={saved} onViewStateChange={setSaved}>...</ViewStateProvider>
```

`viewState` is an opaque `Record<string, unknown>`; persist it as JSON. Without a provider the
underlying `useViewSetting(key, initial)` behaves as plain `useState`.

## Async, loading, error and empty states

`@r4pm/components` exports `AsyncBoundary`, `LoadingState`, `ErrorState`, `EmptyState`,
`IndeterminateBar` and skeletons for the panels around viewers.

## Diagnosing a broken render

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Viewer blank or a few pixels tall | no definite height above it | give an ancestor a height; `flex: 1; min-height: 0` in a flex column |
| Nodes stacked in a line | no layout engine | set `ViewerConfig.layout` |
| Layout right, styling missing | `styles.css` not imported, or `rules.css` before your Tailwind entry | fix imports and order |
| Whole viewport stretched | root `Theme` has `min-height: 100vh` | `<Theme style={{ minHeight: 0 }}>` for embedded use |
| No export button | no `ViewerExportFrame` | wrap the viewer |
| Only "Screenshot" in the export menu | that component registers no vector source, or the frame sits inside the viewer | check the export table; move the frame outward |
| "nothing to export (source produced null)" | `toSvg` ran before layout finished | export once the graph has rendered |
| Export image includes the toolbar | no `data-export-root` | mark the content subtree |
| Colors change every render | `colorOf` rebuilt inline | memoize it |
| Relayout on every render | `data`, `categoryOf` or `layout` identity changes | memoize them |

## Repo commands

```sh
pnpm --filter @r4pm/components dev        # Storybook gallery on :6006
pnpm --filter @r4pm/components showcase   # static Storybook build
pnpm --filter @r4pm/components typecheck
pnpm --filter @r4pm/components docs:types # regenerate data-type docs + this file's tables
pnpm --filter @r4pm/components build
```
